verses.1: How painful it will be for Adonai to throw down Zion from heaven! A beautiful land will be given to Israel, but its blood will not be remembered on that day.
verses.2: In his exile, Jacob’s desires were destroyed. He was taken away from the land of the Jews. He arrived in a land without a king or rulers.
verses.3: He struck with his sword all the branches of Israel. He turned around to his right side, away from the enemy. And Jacob was like fire that burned brightly. It consumed everything around him.
verses.4: His path was difficult; he stood there like a victim. All those who were eager to see him died in the tomb of Zion’s daughter. His fire consumed them all.
verses.5: Adonai was like a destroyer who plundered Israel, destroying all its cities. He multiplied the sins of the Jews.
verses.6: And he neglected the gardens that were meant to be used for worship. He forgot about Jehovah during the festivals of Passover and Shavu’t. In his anger, he rebelled against the king and the priests.
verses.7: May Adonai be abandoned; may his holy place be desecrated. May its palaces be turned into ruins. May the voices of those who worshiped there be silenced in the house of Jehovah today.
verses.8: God thought of destroying the house of Zion. He refused to return his hand from the destruction. They wept together in sorrow.
verses.9: Their gates were destroyed on the earth; their palaces were broken apart. Their kings and queens were taken captive in other lands. There was no more any rule or prophet among them. They did not find any sign from Jehovah.
verses.10: They sat down on the ground. The elders of Zion rose up. They put sashes around their heads. Then they threw their heads back onto the ground, in Jerusalem.
verses.11: All my eyes are filled with tears; they flow down onto the earth. I am like a flower that has been trampled underfoot. My people’s daughter is covered in blood, and she lies there, bleeding profusely.
verses.12: To their mothers, they would say, “Where are the fish and shrimps? They’re trapped in the chaos of the city streets. Their souls are lost in the chaos of the city.”
verses.13: What can I testify to you? You have gone to Jerusalem. You have gone to Zion. I comfort you in the place where the daughter of Zion is. She is like the sea that brings peace. Who can heal you?
verses.14: Your prophets have seen your suffering and cried out for help, but they did not give you any hope of recovery. They saw that you were in a state of despair.
verses.15: They have taken over your shoulders. All those who were on the road have fled. Their heads are now in Jerusalem, this city that was said to be the most beautiful city in all of the world.
verses.16: Their mouths were full of your enemies. They howled and screamed. They said, “We will destroy you!” But today, we have found him. We have seen him.
verses.17: Yahweh did as He had promised. He destroyed those who obeyed His words from ancient times. He did not spare them, but He rejoiced over you. Oh, how great is Your glory!
verses.18: Their hearts cried out to the Lord of Hotham, daughter of Zion. May the river of tears flow day and night! Please do not let me suffer like this. Do not allow your eyes to weep.
verses.19: Get up in the night to carry out my commands. Let the waters flow down upon you. Be present before Adonai, with your hands raised over your broken spirit. They are covered in hunger, from head to toe.
verses.20: Look, LORD! See whom you have sinned against. If women eat the fruit of these trees, they will be considered sinners. And if a priest or prophet is killed in the holy place, that too will be considered a sin.
verses.21: They lay down on the ground, young men and old women. They fell in the fields and in the ravines. You killed them on that day. You did not care at all.
verses.22: It will be called today, “The Day of the Exiles from All Around.” And it wasn’t in that day that Jehovah showed mercy and compassion towards those who were oppressed and suffered.
